findings.location: Scope; Increment B and Increment D, versus docs/specs/knowledge-base.md “Assumptions and constraints”
findings.problem: The helper exposes a command that sends agent-supplied project text to the embedding server, but the named spec says an agent may run only reads that change nothing and send nothing out. The plan acknowledges the transmission but neither resolves this direction conflict nor includes the required owner checkpoint for changing what the spec says about direction.
findings.suggestion: Before implementation, obtain and record the owner’s direction on permitting this networked helper call, then explicitly update the governing spec/policy and add the required checkpoint to the plan.

findings.location: Assumptions and constraints; Increment A, step 1
findings.problem: The plan requires replies to fit the helper’s 65,536-character bound without helper truncation, but specifies only a fixture-based under-60,000-character test. It defines no runtime output budget or behavior for real cards whose rendered result data makes the JSON exceed that limit. The existing helper silently cuts oversized output, which can produce an incomplete, invalid JSON reply.
findings.suggestion: Specify and test an engine-enforced serialized-output budget below the helper limit, including deterministic behavior when it would be exceeded (for example, a bounded result representation or a refusal before printing).

summary: The plan has one unresolved governing-spec conflict and lacks an enforceable output-size guarantee.
